title: Sale Banner Maker for Square Offer Images | AIVideosUGC
description: Move stock with a seasonal sale image that leaves clean space for your offer. One product photo becomes a square banner; add discount and dates in Canva.
h1: Sale Banner Maker with Open Space for Offer Text
lead: A discount with no clear sale image gets lost in crowded feeds, and custom banner design for every event takes time you do not have. Upload one product photo and this sale banner maker places it in a seasonal scene with a calm open area ready for your discount, dates and code.
benefits_h2: Why use an AI sale banner maker?

benefits.t: Offer space built into the scene
benefits.d: The product sits to one side with open sky, wall or snow deliberately left clear. Your discount and dates have a clean place to land without covering the item.
Because the offer is a separate text layer, the same photo can run a percent-off headline, a free-shipping message or a code in different ads. Update the deal without commissioning a new banner.
Describe a darker Black Friday scene, end-of-season clearance or a holiday fireplace setting. The square image fits Facebook and Instagram feeds, then adapts to a 9:16 canvas for Stories.

benefits.t: Numbers stay accurate and yours to use
benefits.d: Type the discount, code and end date yourself so AI never garbles a price. Downloads have no AIVideosUGC watermark and can be used commercially in your own ads.

intro: The example shows a blue hard-shell suitcase beside a pale wall and a small leafy plant, with all wheels visible. The open wall space is the natural place for a sale headline and dates.

A sale image has two jobs: show the product and give the offer a clean place to sit. This handles the first and leaves room for the second, because you'll add the percentage, dates, and code yourself in Canva, where every number stays exact. Use it for Black Friday, end-of-season clearance, and holiday promotions on Facebook and Instagram.

A sale image needs a clean product view and a deliberate place for the offer. A suitcase beside an open wall, a cutting board on a pale counter, or a complete skincare item on a quiet vanity gives the editor space for a discount without hiding the product. Keep the whole silhouette, handles, wheels, and important edges inside the frame before you add campaign text.

Use the template for a feed tile, a product-page promotion, or a seasonal clearance message. Describe the product, the light, and the empty area where the offer will sit; then add the percentage, dates, code, and legal wording in your editor. Separating the offer from the generated scene lets you update the price when stock changes and keeps numbers accurate.

Before the ad goes live, compare the color and model in the image with the product page and inventory. Check that the square crop still shows the full item and that any 9:16 adaptation leaves room for the platform interface. Remove the discount layer when the sale ends, and keep the product image only when the same product and destination remain available.

Plan the offer around the product evidence a shopper needs. For a suitcase, show the wheels and handle; for a cutting board, show the usable surface; for a skincare item, keep the cap and applicator visible. This gives the sale image a clear job before the seasonal props enter the frame.

Use the finished tile only when the destination matches the item shown. For channel guidance, compare [Facebook ad formats](/platforms/facebook-ads), [Instagram ad formats](/platforms/instagram-ads), and the [ad size guide](/guides/ad-sizes-by-platform) before adapting the crop.

For a larger campaign, pair this still with a [feed ad photo](/ai-image-generation/feed-ad-still), a [lifestyle scene](/ai-image-generation/lifestyle-scene), or a [white background photo](/ai-image-generation/ecommerce-main-image). Use the [sale discount occasion](/occasions/sale-discount), [Black Friday occasion](/occasions/black-friday), and [testing ad versions guide](/guides/testing-ad-versions) to keep the offer and destination consistent.
tip: Say where you want the empty space, for example "open sky across the left third," so your offer text has a calm area to sit on.
steps_h2: How to make a sale banner in 3 simple steps
steps_lead: Three steps turn one product photo into an offer-ready sale banner — no designer, no shoot, no wrong prices burned in.

steps.d: Use a clear photo showing the full shape, color and main details. The banner keeps that exact product so shoppers recognize the sale item.
Name the seasonal setting and where the open area should sit. The product is placed clear of the offer zone without a custom design session.
Enter the discount, code and end date in your editor, then post the square banner or adapt it to 9:16. No AIVideosUGC watermark is added.

ideas.d: Darker, dramatic light with plenty of empty space for bold offer text.
Summer dresses on a late-season beach or coats in early spring snow to move last season's stock.
A product by a decorated fireplace or a frosted window for gift ads during the holiday rush.

faq.q: Why doesn't the banner include my discount text?
faq.a: AI-made lettering sometimes garbles words and digits, and a wrong price on a sale ad causes real trouble. Adding the text yourself keeps every figure exact.

faq.q: What size is the sale image?
faq.a: Square by default, which fits Facebook and Instagram feed posts. For a wide website header, set the image on a wider canvas in your design tool.

faq.q: Can I reuse one image for different offers?
faq.a: Yes. Since the offer is added afterward, this image can carry a percent-off headline in one ad and a free-shipping line in another.

faq.q: Can I make a sale banner in a vertical format?
faq.a: The sale template produces a square image by default. Add a 9:16 canvas in your design tool after download if you need a Story or Reel placement.

faq.q: Which placements fit the square sale image?
faq.a: The 1:1 image fits Facebook and Instagram feeds; place it on a 9:16 canvas for Stories and Reels.

faq.q: Can I update the discount without a new photo?
faq.a: Yes. Since the offer is a separate text layer, change the percentage or dates on the same background image.

faq.q: How many credits does a sale photo use?
faq.a: Each photo costs 24 credits and the charge is shown before you run it.

faq.q: Where should I place a discount code?
faq.a: Put the code in the open area as an editable text layer, then check the full offer on a phone-sized preview.

faq.q: How do I remove an expired promotion?
faq.a: Delete or replace the offer layer before reusing the image so an old date or code is never shown.

faq.q: Can I use the sale image without an offer?
faq.a: Yes. Keep the clean product scene for a product-page image or add a different approved message later.

faq.q: Can I run these banners as paid sale ads?
faq.a: Yes. Images you make can be used in your own paid ads, product pages and social posts, with no AIVideosUGC watermark on the download. You are responsible for the offer terms, claims and disclosures in the ad.

faq.q: What happens to the banner when the sale ends?
faq.a: Delete, pause or replace the offer layer so an expired date or code is never shown. The underlying product scene can be reused for a new promotion or kept as a plain listing image.

overview.h2: Give the Offer a Place to Land
overview.p: A sale visual has to show the item and leave enough calm surface for the message. This template creates the scene first, with open sky, wall, snow, or another quiet area that you can use for a percentage, date, code, or shipping line later.

overview.h2: Keep Promotion Facts in Your Hands
overview.p: The generated image supplies seasonal context; your store or design tool supplies the exact offer. Add only an approved discount, date, inventory note, and link after download so a customer never sees a guessed number.

input_guide.h2: Reserve Negative Space Before You Run

items.d: Use a crisp source of the jacket, bag, shoe, or other item that is actually part of the sale.
Say open sky on the left third, a clear wall above the product, or snow behind the subject.
Mention winter, summer, holiday, or end-of-season details that support the campaign without adding a promotion claim.
Keep the item away from the planned text zone so the offer and product can be read separately.

results.h2: A Sale Key Visual Can Provide

items.d: Put the discounted item in a scene that matches the season or campaign mood.
Carry this visual into a percent-off post, free-shipping message, or reminder by changing the overlay.
Use the download in Facebook or Instagram feed creative after verifying the promotion details.
A dark coat or bag on a dramatic charcoal set with open space on the upper right for bold offer text.
A dress or sandal on a late-season beach with bright sky left clear for the date and discount.
A boxed product beside a decorated fireplace with a calm frosted window area for the offer.
A lamp or cushion in a bright room with an uncluttered wall above the product for a short sale line.

after_download.h2: Publish the Offer With Exact Information

items.t: Add the promotion in a design tool
items.d: Type the approved percentage, price, dates, code, and link after the image is downloaded.
Confirm the featured color, size, and stock still match the products the campaign sends people to.
Review feed and mobile placements so the product and offer remain visible together.
